title: Regularization, curvature currents and qualified capacity theories
scope: Fix the original finite extension K/Q_p and its prescribed absolute value. Work on a good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth analytic space of pure dimension n, with ordinary Berkovich opens and all original CLD tests, including their actual refinements. C_b denotes actual locally bounded classical plurisubharmonic functions. A background S is fixed, symmetric, positive in the middle CLD cone, and separately d'- and d''-closed; q = n - p for bidegree (p,p). Each arrow retains the additional local hypotheses printed with it. 'Known' reports a result established in the source; this map does not give independent proof acceptance. Projective metric results retain their smooth projective, ample-line and regular- or normal-model hypotheses. The continuous moving-background theorem is in its stated smooth quasi-projective scope. Ambient Choquet results use [1] and the specified negative exhaustion; parameter-band results retain their annihilation and seed-family conditions. Known includes internally supplied foundational results in the sources.
reviewStatus: Source fidelity checked; no new independent proof acceptance

nodes.title: Regularization on one fixed neighborhood
nodes.summary: Bounded classical potentials admit decreasing continuous semipositive rational PL approximants over the original field. Finite families share one ordinary neighborhood. Continuous members admit smooth positive uniform approximants; smooth majorants used in the collar argument need not form a decreasing row.

nodes.title: Finite control of original test coefficients
nodes.summary: A positive current has Radon coefficient measures. On each compact original test presentation, one positive trace controls all coefficient variations and bounded Borel multiplication. Positivity and the estimate survive actual moment refinements, including rank drops.

nodes.title: Ordered bounded products exist
nodes.summary: The recursion T(S,k) = D(u_1 T(S,k-1)) gives positive, separately closed coefficient-Radon currents. At this stage the order of the differentiated slots is retained; permutation symmetry and joint decreasing continuity are proved later.

nodes.title: Common collars and two trace bounds
nodes.summary: On smaller norm boxes, all relevant potentials can be patched to the same smooth psh collar. Green exchange with a smooth argument gives a lower trace bound; continuous majorants give a separate upper bound for decreasing weights. The limits are arranged with a fixed coefficient measure at each discontinuous multiplication.

links.label: Lemma 3.5: upper bound for decreasing weights

nodes.title: Weighted joint decreasing continuity
nodes.summary: For a fixed allowed background and locally bounded decreasing classical potentials, the mixed products converge with an additional undifferentiated classical psh weight. Convergence holds on every original compact smooth complementary test, not merely on a selected trace family.

nodes.title: Symmetric bounded calculus and CLN bounds
nodes.summary: Ordered products become symmetric in their potential slots, while retaining positivity, separate closedness, ordinary locality and weighted decreasing continuity. Relative CLN bounds control compact coefficient mass. This node does not yet assert that changing a potential while preserving its curvature leaves every background product unchanged.

nodes.title: Quantitative relative capacity estimate
nodes.summary: For a bounded decreasing row with one fixed smooth collar, the capacity of {u_j-u > delta} is bounded by C/delta times a fixed-measure error to the power 2^(-k). Thus the row converges in relative capacity on that norm-box domain.

nodes.title: Local capacity convergence and quasicontinuity
nodes.summary: Bounded decreasing classical potentials converge in relative capacity on a smaller norm-box core. Every bounded classical potential is continuous outside an ordinary open set of arbitrarily small relative capacity. In top degree the capacity needs no auxiliary trace form.

nodes.title: Separate bounded-difference criterion
nodes.summary: For an actual function h locally expressible as a difference of bounded classical psh functions, D[h] is positive if and only if h itself is classical psh. This is a separately adopted analytic input, with curve order transfer and recovery of the actual upper-semicontinuous representative.

nodes.title: Actual curvature kernel and background order
nodes.summary: The kernel on bounded classical differences consists of actual continuous functions whose two signs are classical psh. Curvature order D[u] >= D[v] transfers to D(uS) >= D(vS); equality therefore permits replacement of any potential slot by another with the same curvature.

nodes.title: Products glue from local curvature potentials
nodes.summary: When each curvature current locally has a bounded classical potential, the local mixed products agree on overlaps. They define a unique positive, separately closed, symmetric product of those curvature currents and the chosen background.

links.label: Corollary 4.4: products of locally potential currents

nodes.title: Continuous curvature relations descend
nodes.summary: Finite continuous-coefficient relations between degree-one curvature currents remain relations after inserting a fixed positive closed background. Applying this one slot at a time gives a well-defined positive symmetric mixed operation on the continuous curvature module.

links.label: Theorem 5.1: continuous relation transfer and proof

nodes.title: Locality on strict maximum regions
nodes.summary: The mixed current of max(u,v) agrees with that of u on the Borel region {u > v}, and analogously on {v > u}. These regions need not be ordinary open, so ordinary restriction locality alone does not give this statement.

links.label: R4: maximum locality for a fixed background

nodes.title: Comparison under a compact boundary gap
nodes.summary: If the ordinary closure of every strict gap {u < v-epsilon} is compactly contained in V, then the top relative measure of v on {u < v} is at most that of u there. The proof uses maximum locality and the bounded calculus; it requires no capacity theorem or strictly psh exhaustion.

links.label: R4: relative comparison with compact boundary gap

nodes.title: Domination and uniqueness modulo capacity zero
nodes.summary: With the required compact gaps, zero u-mass on {u < v} forces that set to have zero relative capacity. Equal relative Monge–Ampere measures, with gaps in both orders, force {u != v} to have zero relative capacity. Neither conclusion alone identifies pointwise representatives.

nodes.title: Additional condition: detect every strict gap
nodes.summary: For the proposed pair (S,V), every nonempty strict gap {a < b-delta} of admissible bounded classical potentials with compact gaps must have positive relative capacity. Establishing useful intrinsic hypotheses remains part of CAP-DETECT. The condition fails for S = 0 and can fail away from a nonzero background's support.

links.label: R4: the exact additional detection condition
Open Problem 5.2: tester recovery and relative detection

nodes.title: Pointwise order and uniqueness, conditionally
nodes.summary: Once strict-gap detection is supplied for (S,V), the preceding capacity-zero conclusions imply u >= v, or u = v in the uniqueness case. The conditional implication is proved; the required detection property is not asserted for arbitrary positive closed backgrounds.

links.label: R4: conditional pointwise conclusion and proof

nodes.title: Outer capacity on arbitrary Borel sets
nodes.summary: For every strict Laurent box and allowed extending background, is the relative outer capacity of each Borel set the supremum of its values on compact subsets? The question includes passage from relatively compact sets to an exhaustion. Counterexamples to raw/outer equality, strong subadditivity and extremal total-mass calibration do not refute this Borel inner-regularity question.

links.label: Open Question 5.1: Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity
The exact outer-capacity equality being asked
Known finite-Hausdorff saturated range and proposed remainder route

nodes.title: Continuous calculus for approachable potentials
nodes.summary: For continuous potentials already locally approximable uniformly by smooth positive potentials, insertion into a positive separately closed background preserves positivity and closedness. It is jointly continuous for locally uniform potentials and weakly converging positive closed backgrounds; successive insertions are symmetric.

links.label: R: a fixed approachable potential and proof

nodes.title: One normalized complete-intersection curve at a time
nodes.summary: On a smooth projective variety, a mixed current of uniform Fubini–Study limits on ample lines is a weak limit of individual normalized smooth complete-intersection curves over the original field. Every member retains the specified normalized intersection degrees.

nodes.title: Zero contact identifies the upper metric
nodes.summary: A finite continuous curve-positive metric above a uniform Fubini–Study lower metric on an ample line equals it when their gap has zero integral against the lower Monge–Ampere measure. Only the lower metric needs its higher-dimensional product in advance.

links.label: R: contact rigidity and its three proof steps

nodes.title: Uniform test-ideal control on a regular model
nodes.summary: Weighted test ideals give one degree-independent vertical error and global generation after one fixed ample twist. After dividing weights by their degree, the error is O(1/m). These are the algebraic estimates used to construct the regular-model envelope.

nodes.title: Continuous orthogonal envelopes on regular models
nodes.summary: For a regular integral projective flat model with smooth generic fibre and an ample rational line, every finite continuous obstacle has a continuous orthogonal envelope and uniform pure-Fubini–Study approximation. Model obstacles have the stated one-sided O(1/m) approximation.

links.label: R: regular-model envelope theorem and proof

nodes.title: Four equivalent forms of projective semipositivity
nodes.summary: Under the regular-model and ample-line hypotheses, curve positivity, positivity of the original CLD Chern current, uniform Fubini–Study approximability, and uniform approximation by global smooth positive metrics are equivalent for a finite continuous metric.

links.label: R: projective curve criterion and proof

nodes.title: One fixed vertical correction on a normal model
nodes.summary: On the specified normal model, one power of the uniformizer corrects test-ideal subadditivity for every coherent ideal pair and rational exponent. The exponent is chosen before those ideals and exponents; regular-model uncorrected subadditivity alone does not provide this assertion.

links.label: B: global fixed correction and proof
B: finite projections and the vertical different

nodes.title: Ample envelopes through a normal model
nodes.summary: For a smooth projective geometrically integral generic fibre and an ample line, the continuous-obstacle envelope is continuous, model-semipositive on the same line, uniformly approximable by nef rational model metrics, and orthogonal. Its proof uses the separate fixed-correction theorem.

links.label: B: normal-model envelope theorem and proof

nodes.title: Continuous products with moving backgrounds
nodes.summary: For finite continuous current-positive potentials on a smooth quasi-projective analytification, mixed products are symmetric and depend only on their curvature currents. Locally uniform convergence of potentials and weak convergence of positive closed backgrounds give joint continuity, including nets.

nodes.title: Etale compatibility for specified potential tuples
nodes.summary: For an etale map, pull back the specified bounded classical potentials and pass their continuous regularizations to the weighted mixed product upstairs. The result is independent of those regularizations and compatible with restriction and composition; it constructs no pullback of an arbitrary singular current.

nodes.title: Finite-etale degree and descent of a given function
nodes.summary: A finite etale map of constant degree d pushes a pulled-back weighted or unweighted ambient mixed product to d times the base product. A real function already given on the base is bounded classical if its pullback along a finite etale surjection is; this does not glue unrelated functions on different sheets.

links.label: B: descent of the given bounded class
B: the distinction from independent sheet data

nodes.title: Intrinsic differentials on the existing PS module
nodes.summary: Finite actual tangentially compatible piecewise-smooth coefficients times allowed closed currents have intrinsic coefficient-Radon derivatives. The corrected bounded-potential insertion agrees with inserting into each closed tail, is independent of the chosen presentation, and retains the stated differential and symmetry identities. General higher delta-form relation descent is not included.

links.label: S07: reconstruction with its independent cap hypotheses

nodes.title: Faithful completion for fixed local order gauges
nodes.summary: Completing the continuous curvature module in fixed positive local gauges gives faithful actual coefficient-Radon currents and a unique local positive order-continuous mixed action. Different controls are reconciled by a common sum. This completion is a specified subspace, with no identification with all positive currents or the strong first-energy space.

links.label: Theorem 6.3: extension of the mixed operation

nodes.title: Closed bands and original conditional currents
nodes.summary: When all parameter differentials annihilate the background, Borel parameter restrictions stay separately closed and commute with bounded BT insertion. On a second-countable ordinary domain they disintegrate into conditional currents on the original analytic space, with one exceptional set for all original tests and refinements.

nodes.title: A qualified band-capacity completion
nodes.summary: Starting from countable Borel-band combinations of globally continuous classical branches, local outer-capacity closure gives a complete quasicontinuous class with intrinsic bounded mixed currents. For the seed capacity, completed and seed outer capacities coincide. This does not identify all bounded-classical band testers with the seed family or prove raw/outer equality on compact sets.

links.label: Exact outer-capacity statement and its limits

nodes.title: Ambient input N: envelopes and negligible defects
nodes.summary: For the ambient background [1], the defect between the supremum of a locally uniformly upper-bounded classical family and its ordinary upper regularization is locally outer-null. Increasing families have no jump at ambient divisorial points. Local and fixed-domain null ideals are compared through the stated separate theorem.

links.label: R4: negligible sets have ambient outer capacity zero

nodes.title: Ambient input E: open and compact extremals
nodes.summary: For an ordinary open G compactly contained in the specified negative-exhaustion domain V, its extremal equals -1 on G, has ordinary zero boundary value and compactly supported Monge–Ampere measure, and its total mass equals the capacity of G. Compact extremals have the corresponding total-mass identity.

nodes.title: Ambient outer-null, polar and negligible sets
nodes.summary: An outer-null subset of a relatively compact core has a nontrivial pole witness on the qualified exhaustion domain. Local ambient outer-nullity, local pluripolarity and local negligibility therefore agree. A single global pole witness on an arbitrary analytic space is not asserted.

nodes.title: Outer capacity equals ambient extremal total mass
nodes.summary: For every arbitrary subset A of a relatively compact core in the qualified domain, its ambient outer capacity is the total Monge–Ampere mass of the upper-regularized extremal U_A. This theorem does not assume A is Borel or identify raw and outer capacity beforehand.

links.label: Arbitrary-set extremal total-mass formula and proof

nodes.title: Increasing continuity on arbitrary ambient sets
nodes.summary: On each fixed relatively compact core, ambient outer capacity is continuous from below on arbitrary increasing sets. The proof uses increasing ordinary open sublevel covers of extremals, not a Borel-cover substitution for the ordinary-open definition.

links.label: Increasing continuity and its ordinary-open proof

nodes.title: Qualified ambient Choquet and Borel regularity
nodes.summary: On a fixed relatively compact core of the specified exhaustion domain, ambient outer capacity is a finite Choquet capacity. Suslin sets are capacitable; Borel sets have equal raw and outer capacities. These conclusions retain S=[1] and the domain hypotheses.

links.label: Local Choquet capacitability and Borel regularity

hypotheses: Use the continuous arbitrary-background positivity theorem of R, transported to the local analytic setting as in B.
The background is fixed and allowed; the potentials and their limits are locally bounded classical psh, with k <= q.
relations.explanation: For continuous p_j decreasing to u, the continuous theorem makes D(p_j R) positive. Bounded convergence against the fixed coefficient measures gives p_j R -> uR; differentiation and closedness of the positive cone give D(uR). Iteration uses the resulting positive closed current as the next background. This is the construction stage, before permutation symmetry.

hypotheses: Shrink to nested polynomial norm boxes around a compact original test and retain every coordinate used by that test.
All finitely many potential families have one local bound and one projective extension collar; use the smooth regularized maximum with its exact inactive branch.
The lower trace estimate compares coordinatewise ordered potentials. The upper estimate assumes locally bounded decreasing weights and positive currents already convergent on all original tests.
relations.explanation: Patch the potentials to one smooth psh function near the derivative support of a cutoff. Green exchange moves a smooth majorant into a differentiated slot. Successive fixed-background limits give trace monotonicity; continuous majorants and coefficient control give the complementary upper bound for decreasing weights.

hypotheses: All k differentiated rows and the undifferentiated weight decrease to locally bounded classical psh limits on a common neighborhood.
The background stays fixed and 0 <= k <= q; the test is any original compact smooth complementary form.
relations.explanation: Induct on k. Weighted convergence in degree k-1 gives unweighted convergence in degree k after differentiation. The two collar trace bounds identify the weighted degree-k limit. Positive tests of the form C times a trace plus or minus the given test then recover convergence on every original test.

hypotheses: Use symmetry of the continuous arbitrary-background products, obtained by smooth uniform approximation.
For CLN bounds, work between nested compact cutoff neighborhoods and bound each potential there; k <= q.
relations.explanation: Continuous regularizations satisfy permutation symmetry; joint decreasing continuity passes that identity to bounded potentials. The coefficient CLN bound is obtained separately from the ordered recursion: integrate by parts through nested cutoffs, gaining one potential sup norm per slot. No curvature-quotient assertion is used in either argument.

hypotheses: Omega is the interior of one polynomial norm box; a compact L lies in a strictly smaller nested box.
The row u_j decreases to u, is uniformly bounded near L, and u_j = u = one smooth psh h on Omega minus L.
Fix the allowed background, a smooth trace form beta when k < q, and 1 <= k <= q.
relations.explanation: The bounded calculus first yields relative energy measures, Green's identity and Cauchy–Schwarz. For g_j = u_j-u and normalized testers v, these give I_r squared <= A_r I_(r-1), with A_r uniformly bounded by relative CLN. Iterate to exponent 2^(-k), use the level-set bound, and let I_0 tend to zero against the single fixed measure (Du)^k S beta^(q-k).

links.label: R4: relative energy measures and proof

hypotheses: The decreasing family is defined on a neighborhood of the closure of a sufficiently small norm box Omega; V_0 is a smaller relatively compact core.
Keep the admissibility domain and relative capacity fixed, and use its countable subadditivity.
relations.explanation: Patch the entire family to the common collar and apply the quantitative estimate on the core. For a continuous decreasing regularization, choose a subsequence whose exceptional capacities are summable. The union of its ordinary open error sets has arbitrarily small capacity; outside that union the subsequence converges uniformly, so its limit is continuous.

hypotheses: Use actual bounded classical differences, rather than representatives modulo an almost-everywhere relation.
For background order, u and v are bounded classical potentials and p < n; a mixed replacement uses a positive closed mixed tail with total degree at most n.
relations.explanation: Positive D[u-v] makes the actual difference u-v classical psh by the separate criterion; first-order positivity then gives D((u-v)S) >= 0. Equality follows in both orders, and symmetry moves any chosen slot to the front. For the kernel, apply the criterion to both signs: both are upper semicontinuous, hence the actual function is continuous; pointedness gives the converse.

hypotheses: Each input current locally has a potential a_i in C_b with alpha_i = D[a_i]; the chosen background is fixed and k <= q.
On overlaps, the two local potentials represent the same actual curvature current.
relations.explanation: Replace the local potentials one slot at a time on each overlap. Background invariance identifies the mixed currents, and the sheaf property of currents glues them uniquely. Positivity, symmetry and separate closedness pass from the local bounded products.

hypotheses: Use finite presentations A = sum f_i D[g_i], with f_i continuous and g_i in C_b; equality and positivity are those of actual original currents.
The mixed degree remains at most n; other curvature slots and the background are positive when positivity is asserted.
relations.explanation: Freeze the continuous coefficients on small neighborhoods. The bounded-difference criterion converts each positive frozen curvature combination into a classical psh potential, so first-order positivity transfers it to the background. Finite coefficient control makes the freezing error tend to zero. Transfer zero relations one slot at a time to obtain presentation independence; the same estimate proves positivity of the mixed operation.

links.label: Theorem 5.1 and the mixed-operation proof following it

hypotheses: The background is fixed, u, v and the remaining slots lie in C_b, and 1 <= k <= q.
Borel restrictions are coefficient-measure restrictions; no closedness of a restricted current is asserted.
relations.explanation: On continuous approximants, ordinary locality gives h_j A_j = h_j B_j for h_j = max(u_j,v_j)-v_j. Pass to the limit by subtracting two applications of weighted decreasing continuity; the differences h_j need not decrease. The resulting identity h(A-B)=0 can be divided by h on {h >= 1/m}; a countable union recovers {u > v}.

links.label: R4: proof of strict maximum locality

hypotheses: q >= 1 and u,v belong to C_b(V). For every epsilon > 0, the ordinary closure of {u < v-epsilon} is compact and contained in V.
The background is defined and separately closed throughout V; use the top relative measures mu_a = T(S,q)(a,...,a).
relations.explanation: Put w = max(u,v-epsilon). The mixed telescoping identity writes mu_w-mu_u = D((w-u)Q), with compact support. A cutoff makes its total signed mass zero. Maximum locality identifies the measures on the two strict regions; positivity controls the equality region. Let epsilon decrease to zero. This argument does not pass through quasicontinuity or a capacity theorem.

hypotheses: Choose the relevant conclusion. Domination requires compact gaps in the order (u,v) and mu_u({u < v}) = 0. Uniqueness instead requires compact gaps in both orders and mu_u = mu_v as Radon measures.
Capacity uses the full normalized classical tester family 0 <= h <= 1 on the same V.
relations.explanation: Perturb the comparison potential by epsilon(h-1)-delta. Positivity of the mixed expansion exposes the term epsilon^q mu_h on a smaller strict gap. Comparison forces its mass to vanish for every normalized tester; taking the supremum and a countable union gives capacity zero. For uniqueness, cancel only finite masses on compact gaps and then repeat in the other order.

hypotheses: Supply strict-gap detection for the same pair (S,V) and actual classical representatives.
Retain the corresponding domination assumptions, or the equal-measure and two-sided-gap assumptions for uniqueness.
relations.explanation: A prohibited pointwise inequality would hold with some positive margin. Its nonempty strict gap would have positive capacity by the extra condition, contradicting the capacity-zero conclusion. The implication is proved; supplying detection for a proposed geometric class is the open obligation.

hypotheses: Fix a strict Laurent box V, q >= 1, and an allowed background S extending to a neighborhood of its closure. Use outer capacity C*_S and the full family of actual normalized classical testers defined on this same V.

One proposed sufficient local route remains to be proved: for a relatively compact Borel E and each epsilon > 0, find a compact H contained in E and an ordinary open G containing E minus H whose mass is below epsilon uniformly for every actual normalized tester measure.

Separately justify passage to an exhaustion of V while preserving the full tester family and the uniform estimates; a countable dominating-measure reduction or replacement by completed sources needs its own theorem.
relations.explanation: The established convergence and quasicontinuity results provide the local capacity calculus, but do not supply uniform Borel remainders across the entire tester family. The finite-Hausdorff saturated model proves such a remainder estimate in a restricted range and suggests this route. Its extension and the exhaustion step remain open. Failure of raw/outer equality or strong subadditivity blocks shortcuts, not CAP-BOREL itself.

Uniform tester remainders in the restricted positive case

hypotheses: Work in the continuous theory on a smooth quasi-projective analytification over the original valued field; every potential already admits locally uniform smooth positive approximants on a fixed smaller neighborhood.
All backgrounds in the net are positive and separately closed of the same bidegree; the total mixed degree is at most n.
relations.explanation: For a smooth approximant, D(u_j T)=Du_j wedge T is positive. Continuous coefficient control passes locally uniform approximation and weak background limits through multiplication, then differentiation. Iteration and simultaneous smooth approximation give symmetry. This foundational step assumes approachability; it does not first need the current-positivity regularization theorem.

hypotheses: Y is smooth projective of dimension n>=2; the n-1 line bundles are ample rational lines and their metrics are uniform Fubini–Study limits.
Use characteristic-zero Bertini over K, the original calibrated Poincare–Lelong formula, and the total-variation nullity of tie hyperplanes for each smooth test.
relations.explanation: Choose generating sections with prescribed distinct coefficient valuations. For each smooth test, ties have zero mass eventually and the one-cut Poincare–Lelong error is O(1/N). Successive smooth cuts and continuity in the positive background give a net of individual normalized complete-intersection curves. Normalized degrees are preserved algebraically at every cut.

hypotheses: Y is smooth projective integral of positive dimension; L is ample; the lower metric p is a uniform Fubini–Study limit and the upper metric r is finite continuous and positive on every smooth algebraic curve map.
Assume r>=p and integral (r-p)c1(L,p)^n = 0. Use curve Green identities and the smooth-divisor concentration lemma; in dimension one use the curve argument directly.
relations.explanation: Normalized curves give positive upper comparison measures with controlled total variation. Zero contact makes the mixed energy vanish; testing its quadratic perturbation annihilates the mixed Laplacian. Divisor concentration transfers contact to smooth hyperplane sections, and dimension induction plus density of rigid points proves r=p.

links.label: R: concentration on a smooth divisor

hypotheses: The model is regular, integral, projective and flat over the original valuation ring, with smooth generic fibre; L is an ample rational line and the obstacle is finite continuous.
Use density of model metrics, the envelope Lipschitz estimate, and the cited orthogonality theorem for geometrically reduced generic fibres, with its measure identified with the CLD product.
relations.explanation: Global generation produces Fubini–Study metrics on the degree-m line plus a fixed auxiliary line. A fixed complementary generating tuple removes that twist. The test-ideal bounds and the envelope property give a one-sided O(1/m) error for model obstacles. Uniform density extends continuity and approximation to continuous obstacles; the cited orthogonality theorem supplies the contact integral.

links.label: R: envelope proof and cited orthogonality input

hypotheses: Retain the regular integral projective flat model, smooth positive-dimensional generic fibre, ample line and finite continuous metric r.
Use smooth approximation of Fubini–Study metrics and the curve-restriction theorem for a current-positive continuous weight; clear any rational tensor denominator.
relations.explanation: For curve-positive r, the envelope p is semipositive, lies below r and is orthogonal. Contact rigidity forces r=p. Smooth Fubini–Study approximation then gives smooth positive approximation and current positivity; curve restriction closes the reverse implication. The envelope and contact results are joint inputs.

hypotheses: Use a normal integral projective flat model over the complete mixed-characteristic valuation ring, with smooth projective geometrically integral generic fibre and ample L.
After the specified canonical-sheaf modification, choose an effective vertical Delta_0 with K+Delta_0 Cartier; use the stated test-ideal birational, summation and generation theorems.
Use density of model metrics and the cited envelope orthogonality theorem; no regular-model resolution hypothesis is silently imposed on this normal-model proof.
relations.explanation: Iterating the same fixed vertical correction gives an O(1/m) lower estimate for weighted asymptotic test ideals. A fixed birational upper error and one fixed ample generation twist give the upper estimate. Cancelling the auxiliary line and dividing by degree gives uniform approximation on the original identified L; density and orthogonality finish the continuous-obstacle statement.

hypotheses: Use the continuous part of local regularization on a smooth quasi-projective analytification: every finite continuous input has positive original curvature current.
Potentials converge locally uniformly and backgrounds converge weakly on every original compact smooth test, remain positive and separately closed, and have one fixed bidegree.
relations.explanation: Regularization places each current-positive continuous potential in the approachable class. Iterate the foundational moving-background operation. If two potentials have equal curvature, their continuous difference and its negative are both approachable; positivity and pointedness force zero insertion of that difference against every allowed closed tail.

links.label: R: mixed-current theorem proof, including nets and the kernel

hypotheses: f:Y->X is etale between the allowed analytic spaces. A specified tuple u_0,...,u_k lies in C_b on one base ordinary open, with simultaneous decreasing continuous semipositive regularizations there.
Use the ambient integration backgrounds [1] on each space, the original pullback identity for smooth forms, and k<=n.
relations.explanation: At continuous stages, locally uniform smooth approximation identifies the pulled-back operation with the product of the pulled-back weights. Weighted decreasing continuity on Y gives the bounded limit on every original test. Reusing the same approximants proves compatibility with composition and ordinary restriction.

hypotheses: For the degree formula, f is finite etale of constant degree d, and all potentials are specified bounded classical functions on the base; locally constant degrees are handled componentwise.

For class descent, f is a finite etale surjection and u is one real function already given on the base with u composed with f in C_b. Use the cited finite-surjection descent of classical curve subharmonicity.
relations.explanation: The calibrated finite-map integration formula gives the degree factor for smooth tuples; properness keeps pulled-back tests compact, so continuous approximation and weighted decreasing continuity pass the identity to bounded tuples. For the given base function, closedness of the finite map descends upper semicontinuity and local boundedness; curve subharmonicity descends separately.

links.label: B: descent proof for a given base function

hypotheses: Use the established actual codimension-zero PS multiplication, tangency and anchored finite Courant-word presentation, together with the uniform normal-wall variation estimate.
R is a finite sum alpha_nu wedge S_nu, with actual tangentially compatible piecewise-smooth forms alpha_nu and allowed positive separately closed tails S_nu; R itself need not be closed or symmetric.
Inserted potentials are actual locally bounded classical psh; in bidegree (a,b), the mixed insertion budget is max(a,b)+k<=n. No general variable-PS higher delta-form quotient is assumed.
relations.explanation: Simultaneously convolve the finite PL generators. Normal-factor errors are O(epsilon^(1/2)) uniformly over the relevant positive BT tails. First pass weighted BT limits against a fixed smooth test, then remove smoothing. Distributional differentiation makes the derivatives intrinsic. The corrected insertion cancels derivatives of the coefficient current and becomes the sum of the same coefficients times D(uS_nu), proving witness independence.

hypotheses: In each local slot choose a fixed positive represented gauge Q_i, and take an order-Cauchy sequence in its order ideal of symmetric coefficient-Radon (1,1) currents; the number of slots is at most n-p.

Use finitely many common local controls, rather than asserting one global gauge. To conclude separate closedness of the limiting product, require its approximating mixed products to be separately closed.
relations.explanation: Decompose each controlled signed factor into the positive factors (M_i Q_i plus or minus A_i)/2 and telescope differences to get the sharp order bound. Finite test domination realizes order-Cauchy rows as actual currents; weak closedness of the cone proves faithfulness and isometry. Passing the mixed action to limits gives a unique extension, and replacing two choices of control by their sum proves independence and local gluing.

hypotheses: Let s=(log|f_i|) for original analytic units and let R be an allowed symmetric positive separately closed coefficient-Radon current with both d′s_i wedge R=0 and d″s_i wedge R=0.
For the Borel commutation identity, u is locally bounded Borel and D(uR) is coefficient-Radon; bounded classical BT potentials satisfy this requirement.

For conditional currents, work on a second-countable ordinary U and use Radon measure disintegration with the proved countably cofinal original-test system. No rank, submersion, product-chart or fiber-field hypothesis is substituted for these conditions.
relations.explanation: The smooth chain rule kills every parameter derivative by annihilation. One Borel L1 approximation against the coefficient measures of R and D(uR) passes the identities to Borel bands. A countable control measure then permits simultaneous disintegration of original coefficients. Countably cofinal tests impose positivity, closedness and refinement identities outside one null set; continuity recovers every original test. The conditional currents live on U and are carried by its level sets.

links.label: Closed-band theorem and Borel commutation proof
Disintegration on the original ambient space

hypotheses: Retain parameter annihilation and place the closure of V inside the interior of one compact original affinoid; the background has degree P and remaining degree k=n-P>=1. This construction does not require extension of R across the boundary.

The seed family consists of [0,1]-valued countable Borel parameter-band combinations of globally continuous actual classical psh branches. Distinguish its capacity gamma_0 from gamma_1 for all bounded-classical band testers.
Complete the seed family in local OUTER gamma_i capacity, for the chosen i=0 or 1, modulo the matching locally outer-null ideal. Do not assume gamma_0=gamma_1 or raw/outer equality on compact sets.
relations.explanation: Capacity convergence of the seed rows, together with uniform coefficient estimates by outer capacity, makes the bounded mixed currents Cauchy on every original test. Weighted weak passage and the distributional recursion give positive closed intrinsic limits, independent of rows. For the seed capacity, gamma_0<=completed gamma_0<=outer gamma_0, equality on ordinary opens and equality after outer regularization follow. The larger tester family has only the stated inequalities; its cofinality remains a separate issue.

links.label: Exact capacity identities and remaining cofinality gate

hypotheses: The background is [1]. V is a connected ordinary open with compact closure in a smooth affine algebraic chart, nonempty ordinary boundary, and a bounded continuous negative classical exhaustion rho extending continuously as zero on that boundary.

For a witness, E lies in W compactly contained in V and has fixed-domain ambient outer capacity zero. Use the established ambient increasing calculus, pointwise ambient domination, and local/fixed-domain null comparison.
For the reverse implication use the already established ambient polar-to-outer-null theorem; local equivalence does not assert unrestricted global pole patching.
relations.explanation: Choose decreasing ordinary open covers of E with capacities tending to zero. Their extremals increase; the N and E inputs plus the adopted increasing calculus give a zero-mass upper-regularized limit. Ambient pointwise domination makes that limit zero. No jump at a fixed divisorial point allows a subsequence whose negative sum stays finite there but equals minus infinity on E. The existing polar-null implication and local arguments give the equivalence.

hypotheses: Use S=[1] and the same qualified negative-exhaustion domain. A is any subset of a fixed W compactly contained in V; keep V as the admissibility domain.
Use the total-mass order for bounded negative classical functions with ordinary zero boundary limit; retain the upper-regularized extremal U_A rather than its raw supremum.
relations.explanation: An open cover G gives U_G<=U_A, so total-mass order yields one inequality. Input N says A misses the -1 contact set of U_A only on an outer-null set. The truncation max(-1,U_A/(1-eta)) controls the ordinary open sublevel {U_A<-1+eta}; its mass bound gives the reverse inequality as eta tends to zero. No pole-witness theorem is used.

links.label: Total-mass order used in the proof

hypotheses: A_j are arbitrary increasing subsets of one relatively compact core W in the same qualified domain V, with S=[1].
Use countable outer subadditivity and raw-capacity continuity from below only for Borel sets, in particular ordinary open sets.
relations.explanation: The extremals U_(A_j) decrease. Cover their countably many negligible contact defects by one ordinary open set of arbitrarily small capacity. Its union with {U_(A_j)<-1+eta} gives increasing ordinary open covers. The extremal mass estimate controls their capacities; raw continuity on these opens then gives the desired outer-capacity limit.

hypotheses: Retain S=[1] and a fixed relatively compact ordinary core W in the specified negative-exhaustion domain. This core is locally compact, second countable and metrizable in the fixed finite p-adic algebraic setting.
Use the established outer-capacity continuity from above on decreasing compact sets, compact finiteness, and the classical Choquet capacitability theorem.
relations.explanation: The new increasing continuity supplies the missing Choquet axiom. The arbitrary-set mass formula and compact extremal identity identify raw and outer capacity on compact sets. Choquet capacitability handles Suslin sets. On Borel sets, Radon inner regularity permits interchanging two suprema, yielding raw/outer equality. The qualified ambient theorem leaves the general relative CAP-BOREL question open.

panels.title: Construct the bounded calculus and identify the Borel capacity gap
panels.summary: The construction separates ordered products from the later symmetry theorem. Regularization, coefficient control and collar estimates enter together. The proved capacity branch reaches quasicontinuity; the final open step requires uniform tester remainders and a justified exhaustion passage for Borel outer capacity.

panels.title: Add the difference criterion to descend to curvature currents
panels.summary: The bounded calculus and the separately adopted bounded-difference criterion are joint inputs. They yield background order and local-potential gluing; the continuous module requires an additional coefficient-freezing argument. No arrow derives the difference criterion from the bounded product theorem.

panels.title: Separate comparison from the open pointwise detection step
panels.summary: Comparison follows from maximum locality and compact support, independently of the capacity convergence branch. It yields conclusions modulo relative capacity zero. The last arrow requires the explicitly displayed strict-gap detection condition; arbitrary backgrounds need not satisfy it.

panels.title: Projective metrics: two envelope routes and the curve criterion
panels.summary: Curve approximation gives contact rigidity. Regular-model test ideals independently give orthogonal envelopes; both results are needed for the projective curve criterion. Normal-model envelopes use their separate fixed vertical correction, so no regular-to-normal shortcut is asserted.

panels.title: Continuous moving backgrounds and specified etale tuples
panels.summary: Approachability and coefficient control construct the continuous operation before the full regularization theorem is invoked. Regularization then starts from current positivity. The etale branch instead keeps the actual specified potential tuples and their calibrated ambient products.

panels.title: Different extension mechanisms retain different input classes
panels.summary: The PS module needs the established coefficient multiplication and wall estimates. Order completion needs fixed positive local gauges. Closed parameter bands need annihilation of parameter differentials, and their capacity completion keeps a specified seed family. Each arrow lists its own additional input.

panels.title: Why the qualified ambient case has a Choquet theorem
panels.summary: With S=[1] and the stated negative exhaustion, the no-jump and extremal inputs give a pole witness and, independently, an arbitrary-set mass formula. That formula supplies increasing continuity and the Choquet conclusion. Neither branch proves the corresponding package for every relative background.
